title: Universal Jamming Criticality and Self-Organizing Principles from Disorder to the Limit of Perfect Crystalline Order
authors: Jianhua Zhang, Jiaqi Si, Ning Xu, Hua Tong
abstract: While crystals are defined by periodic order, the nature of amorphous solids remains elusive due to their disordered, diverse, and nonequilibrium structures. Here, we focus on jammed elastic packings and systematically tune structure from crystalline to fully disordered to unveil the universal underlying characteristics. We demonstrate that their mechanical properties are universally governed by jamming criticality, featuring characteristic scaling behaviors near the jamming transition, excepting the singular close-packed point. This is facilitated by random nonaffine elasticity arising from contact-level disorder. Consequently, the jamming density can approach close packing, suggesting a fundamental decoupling between jamming criticality and the glass transition physics. Moreover, we uncover a universal coordination-number distribution and contact hyperuniformity in marginally jammed states, independent of particle-level structure. These findings suggest a general organizing mechanism for emergent rigidity in disordered solids, underscore the broad relevance of jamming physics, and complement principles of mechanical self-organization.
summary: This work investigates how mechanical rigidity emerges universally across disordered solids by tuning structure from crystalline to amorphous. The authors demonstrate that jamming criticality dictates mechanical behavior regardless of particle-level details, suggesting a fundamental decoupling from glass transition physics. They achieve this through detailed simulations analyzing coordination number statistics and structural fluctuations.
main_problem: To understand the universal underlying characteristics governing mechanical rigidity (jamming criticality) in amorphous solids by systematically tuning structural order from crystalline to fully disordered states.
main_result: Mechanical properties are universally governed by jamming criticality, suggesting a fundamental decoupling between this critical behavior and the physics of the glass transition. Universal coordination-number distributions and contact hyperuniformity emerge independent of particle structure.
method: Systematic simulation of jammed elastic packings across varying structural disorder (polydispersity) using quasi-static densification methods.
model_or_system: Jammed elastic packings of frictionless particles in 2D and 3D, modeled with harmonic or Hertzian repulsion. The study spans the entire order-disorder spectrum from perfect crystals to fully disordered states.
key_observables: Excess coordination number ($\Delta Z$), modulus ratio ($G/B$), nonaffine deformation anisotropy ($C_6$), universal coordination-number distribution ($f_z$), and contact hyperuniformity measures ($\sigma^2_Z(L)$, $S_Z(q)$).
important_parameters: Polydispersity ($\eta$) controls structural disorder, and pressure ($p$) tunes the system state relative to jamming transitions ($p_j$).
main_assumptions: The study focuses on zero-temperature jamming; finite-disorder thresholds separating crystal and jamming behaviors are challenged by the results.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams showing distinct regimes (Crystal, Disordered Crystal, Jamming Critical) based on pressure and polydispersity. Other figures compare universal scaling laws for coordination number fluctuations and structure factors across different disorder levels.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the mechanical response by varying structural order ($\eta$) while measuring key observables like $\Delta Z$ and $G/B$, establishing three distinct mechanical regimes, before delving into microscopic diagnostics like nonaffine elasticity and hyperuniformity to prove universality.
why_interesting: While focused on classical mechanics, the concept of universal critical scaling near a jamming transition shares mathematical parallels with phase transitions studied in statistical mechanics, particularly concerning emergent order from disorder.
